Definition: Does the government maintain a digital business register?
Comments: Djibouti's e-government portal describes registration with the Registre du Commerce (RC) through ODPIC, indicating an established business register with online government service information; however, evidence does not confirm fully digital end-to-end nationwide register operations.
redteam_note: Comment wording may not match the score — re-read (needs judgement).
revision_notes: Confirmed. ODPIC's Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) is a centralised, legally mandatory national business register (registration required within one month of incorporation) with online publication of registration certificates via the ODPIC and Guichet Unique websites (verified 2025-26 sources). Registration still requires in-person filing at the one-stop shop, so full end-to-end digital deployment is not evidenced. Score of 4 (Partially deployed) upheld.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital civil register?
Comments: DGPF states it manages and centralizes civil status data (birth, marriage, death records) via “registres d'état civil,” indicating digitization/centralization but not evidenced as fully digital nationwide.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Downgraded. A 2022 UN-ESCWA regional CRVS digitisation survey (Djibouti's own self-reported response) found no national/central civil registration database and answered 'No' on electronic birth/death/marriage records at local civil registration offices; a 2022 UNFPA Arab-states CRVS report similarly describes Djibouti's CRVS as 'very poor', with only three communes connected to a central server. This contradicts the generic DGPF web claim of 'centralised' records used to justify the original score. Recalculated as Under development (3). Flagged for human review given a 2026 Ecofin report on a new Mobile ID platform citing access to 'civil registry records', which may indicate more recent progress not yet independently confirmed via an authoritative technical source.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital electoral register?
Comments: ACE Electoral Knowledge Network profile for Djibouti notes that the electoral register is managed/controlled and includes “computerized transmission of results,” implying digitization elements but not clearly nationwide fully deployed digital electoral register.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Revised down. The cited ACE source refers to computerised transmission of election RESULTS to the Ministry of the Interior, not digitisation of the voter register itself. The governing 2010 CENI decree only describes a 'fichier électoral' without specifying digital format, printed voter cards are still produced and distributed (2026 election reporting), and International IDEA confirms Djibouti's electoral management body does not capture biometric data during voter registration. No authoritative source was found confirming the digitisation status of the electoral register itself, so recalculated as Unknown (0). Flagged for human review to check CENI/ANSIE directly for a named digital voter-register system.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital population register?
Comments: Ministry of Interior's Direction Générale de la Population et de la Famille (DGPF) manages the “Registre National des Personnes Physiques (RNPP)” and states it is establishing a centralized biometric system to register all persons on national territory, suggesting deployment is underway but not evidenced as fully nationwide.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Law n°39/AN/19 (2019) and Decrees 2020-146/2020-150 establish the biometric RNPP and National Identification Number (10 fingerprints, facial image); a December 2025 government budget document confirms ANSIE's ongoing datacentre/X-Road interoperability investment for the RNPP; and a Mobile ID platform (reported by Ecofin, 2026) has since launched, enabling authentication for tax, banking and civil-registry access. No source confirms full nationwide enrolment, so Partially deployed (4) is upheld.

Definition: Does the government maintain one or more social protection registers?
Comments: Ministry of Social Affairs describes the “Registre Social” as a system/database for identifying poor/vulnerable households, using biometrics and generating a unique identification number (NIU), indicating a deployed social registry but not evidenced as fully nationwide single registry for all programs.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and refreshed. Original source (sociales.gouv.dj PDF) could not be re-verified (SSL error). World Bank project documents (2016-2021) corroborate an operational national social registry (run by MASS/ADDS) covering roughly 85,000-90,000 households (over 40% of the population, including refugees since 2020) with proxy-means-test targeting for cash transfers — more recent and detailed evidence than the original 2022 source. Partially deployed (4) upheld; not evidenced as a single fully nationwide registry covering all programmes.
